subject.title: feat: bound raw transcript reads across replacements

question: Should OpenClaw adopt schema v13 generation tokens and a public Plugin SDK raw-transcript cursor as a shared durable foundation, rather than keep bounded inspection as a narrower owner-specific capability?
rationale: This choice fixes the long-term database and external SDK compatibility boundary; tests can validate an approved contract but cannot decide whether that public surface and persistent state should exist.

options.title: Approve the shared foundation
options.body: Accept schema v13 and the bounded raw cursor as a supported Plugin SDK contract, then land only after confirming the documented upgrade and cursor semantics.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Keep the active-memory optimization but redesign it around a smaller owner-specific or existing SDK seam so no broad raw cursor contract or database migration is introduced.

options.title: Defer the API
options.body: Pause the stack until additional concrete consumers justify the durable schema and public cursor surface.

recommendation.title: Approve the shared foundation
recommendation.body: Accept schema v13 and the bounded raw cursor as a supported Plugin SDK contract, then land only after confirming the documented upgrade and cursor semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The assigned author owns the proposed transcript foundation and its declared stacked consumers; a repository owner should make the final product decision with that context.
